memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "About Joseph he said: 'May the Lord bless his land with the precious dew from heaven above and with the deep waters that lie below; with the best the sun brings forth and the finest the moon can yield; with the choicest gifts of the ancient mountains and the fruitfulness of the everlasting hills; with the best gifts of the earth and its fullness and the favor of him who dwelt in the burning bush.'" — Deut 33:13-16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The blessing on Joseph overflows with abundance — dew from heaven, deep waters, the best of sun and moon, the choicest gifts of the mountains, the fullness of the earth. Moses piles up image upon image of God's rich provision. And notice the crowning phrase: "the favor of him who dwelt in the burning bush." The greatest gift in this whole catalogue of blessings is not the produce or the land — it is God's favour, His presence, His face turned toward His people.

That is the true treasure. All the good gifts of creation are wonderful, but they are only meaningful because they come from a God whose favour rests on His people. Better than dew and harvest and mountain riches is the smile of God Himself.

We should be careful, of course, not to read this abundant tribal blessing as a promise that God will make every believer materially wealthy. This was a specific blessing on Joseph's descendants. But it reveals the generous heart of God and, more importantly, teaches us where the greatest blessing truly lies — in God's favour and presence.

And here is the wonder of the gospel: the favour of God, once resting on Joseph, now rests fully on all who are in Christ. In Jesus, God says over us what He said at Jesus' baptism — you are my beloved, with you I am well pleased (Matt 3:17). Through Christ, we have "every spiritual blessing" (Eph 1:3) and, above all, the favour and presence of God. Seek that above every other gift, for it is the best blessing of all.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I treasure God's favour and presence above His other gifts?
2. Am I ever tempted to want the blessings more than the Blesser?
3. How does having God's favour in Christ change what I most desire?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, all Your gifts are good, but the best of all is Your favour and presence. Thank You that in Christ Your face is turned toward me in blessing. Help me treasure You above every other gift. Amen.
